ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the parabola $y=-x^2+2x+1$ intersects the x-axis at points A and B, and intersects the y-axis at point C. Point D is the vertex of the parabola, and the point symmetrical to C with respect to the axis of symmetry of the parabola is point E. Points G and F are located on the x-axis and the y-axis, respectively. What is the minimum perimeter of the quadrilateral EDFG?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
Solution: Let $x=0$, then $y=1$,\\
$\therefore$ $C(0,1)$,\\
$\because$ $y=-x^2+2x+1=-{(x-1)}^2+2$,\\
$\therefore$ $D(1,2)$, the axis of symmetry of the parabola is the line $x=1$,\\
$\because$ the symmetric point of C with respect to the axis of symmetry of the parabola is point E,\\
$\therefore$ $E(2,1)$,\\
$\therefore$ $DE=\sqrt{1^2+1^2}=\sqrt{2}$,\\
Construct the symmetric point ${D}^{\prime }$ of D with respect to the y-axis, and the symmetric point ${E}^{\prime }$ of E with respect to the x-axis, connect ${D}^{\prime }{E}^{\prime }$, intersecting the x-axis at point G and the y-axis at point F, as shown in the figure,\\
Then ${D}^{\prime }(-1,2)$, ${E}^{\prime }(2,-1)$, $FD=F{D}^{\prime }$, $GE=G{E}^{\prime }$,\\
At this time, $DF+FG+EG=F{D}^{\prime }+FG+G{E}^{\prime }={D}^{\prime }{E}^{\prime }$,\\
$\therefore$ At this time, the perimeter of the quadrilateral EDFG is minimal,\\
Extend $D{D}^{\prime }$ and $E{E}^{\prime }$, they intersect at point H, as shown in the figure,\\
Then ${D}^{\prime }H=3$, $H{E}^{\prime }=3$,\\
$\therefore$ ${D}^{\prime }{E}^{\prime }=\sqrt{3^2+3^2}=3\sqrt{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ The minimum perimeter of the quadrilateral EDFG is $DE+DF+FG+EG=DE+{D}^{\prime }{E}^{\prime }=\sqrt{2}+3\sqrt{2}=\boxed{4\sqrt{2}}$.

A downward-opening parabola crosses the x-axis at A on the left and B on the right, crosses the y-axis at C, and has vertex D. The auxiliary points E, F, G, D′, and E′ are not drawn in the visible figure, so their positions are determined from the given equation and conditions. Reasoning: From the equation y = -x^2 + 2x + 1, complete the square: y = -(x - 1)^2 + 2. Thus the vertex is D = (1, 2), and the axis of symmetry is x = 1. Reflect E = (2, 1) across the x-axis to get E′ = (2, -1), so GE = GE′ for any G on the x-axis. Hence DF + FG + GE equals the broken path length D′F + FG + GE′. This is minimized when D′, F, G, and E′ lie on one straight line, giving minimum length D′E′. Compute D′E′ = sqrt((2 - (-1))^2 + (-1 - 2)^2) = sqrt(3^2 + (-3)^2) = 3sqrt(2). Therefore the minimum perimeter of quadrilateral EDFG is DE + D′E′ = sqrt(2) + 3sqrt(2) = 4sqrt(2).
